header:
Date: 2026-02-25
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood Product), Alex Rivera (CTO, Acme Payments), Maria Chen (Head of Security, Acme), Tom Wu (Lead Engineer, Acme)
summary: Redwood demo focused on data handling and retention controls: request storage toggles, logging redaction, PII detection and masking, KMS integration, audit logs, and retention policy automation. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment given regulatory and PCI considerations; interested in short POC to validate retention toggles and redaction during live traffic.
topics: KMS/HSM key control and envelope encryption
Audit logs and access controls (RBAC, SSO)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, i have priya (se) and luis from product with me. can you hear us okay?
[00:07] Alex: Yep loud and clear, thanks. we carved out 45 but 42 is fine.
[00:15] Jordan: Great, quick agenda: we'll show how retention toggles work in Console, API flags to opt-out of request storage, demo redaction pipeline, and a primer on KMS integration and audit logs. then q&a.
[00:28] Maria: Great, from security perspective we're mainly focused on pci scope, piI leakage, and the ability to fully purge data on request.
[00:35] Priya: Perfect, we'll start in the Console. so in the top nav you can see Projects -> Data Controls. I'm going to switch to a demo org for this view. (screen share starts)
[00:47] Priya: Here we have per-route settings; you can toggle Request Storage: store requests / do not store. if you set do not store, request payloads are never written to long-term storage, only ephemeral caches used for inference.
[01:05] Tom: Is that at the route level or global? we have multi-tenant services, want it per-client.
[01:12] Priya: Per-route and per-model. you can also attach a policy to a client id. so your SAAS tenant could be configured to never store.
[01:22] Jordan: Just to clarify, do-not-store means raw request body isn't persisted to disk or object storage, we still emit minimal telemetry for billing and usage (token counts) but can obfuscate or aggregate to remove PII.
[01:35] Maria: Token counts are fine but we need to see redaction for logs - we cannot have card numbers or emails in plaintext in logs.
[01:43] Priya: Absolutely, so we have two layers: logging redaction at ingestion, and PII detection/masking as part of the postprocess pipeline. in ingestion we apply regex based scrubbers and an ML-based PII detector.
[01:55] Priya: i'll toggle it on and send a sample request. (typing) ok sent.
[02:03] Priya: you can see the raw request in dev view but with redaction markers, like <REDACTED_EMAIL> and <REDACTED_CC>. the actual value is purged if retention policy says do-not-store.
[02:18] Alex: How reliable is the ML detector? we have edge cases with tokenized account ids that look like uuids.
[02:26] Priya: Good question. ML detector has precision tuning; you can set sensitivity and an allowlist/denylist. for ambiguous patterns we backfill with regex rules. we also surface a "suspected PII" flag in the audit trail so you can review before purging.
[02:44] Jordan: Also, if you need stronger guarantees, Dedicated or Private deployment gives you the ability to manage keys and logs within your VPC and control storage lifecycle.
[02:54] Tom: can you walk through kms integration? we use AWS KMS for envelope keys and would like HSM backed keys for private deployments.
[03:03] Priya: Sure. we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations for Private. requests are encrypted at rest with envelope encryption; you control the master key. we also support key rotation and we don't retain plaintext keys.
[03:20] Maria: Do logs contain decrypted data? 
[03:24] Priya: No, audit logs contain metadata and redaction markers, not the plaintext. we maintain a separate key access audit for decrypt operations. if you enable the do-not-store toggle, the plaintext is never written to persistent logs.
[03:39] Alex: How about the API? can we flip retention from the request side? say our app makes a call and wants to mark it as ephemeral.
[03:47] Priya: Yes, there's an API header x-redwood-store: never | yes | session. if you send x-redwood-store: never, we honor it at the request layer and skip persisting the request body, only storing the minimal metadata needed for billing.
[04:02] Tom: Are there audit trails to show who toggled a setting? our compliance team needs user-level change history.
[04:09] Priya: Console has RBAC and SSO integrations (SAML/OIDC). every config change is logged with user id, timestamp, and diff. those audit logs can be exported to your SIEM or to an S3 bucket.
[04:23] Jordan: i'll show the audit export flow. (screen) here we click export, choose destination, and choose retention window for the exported logs. you can set lifecycle rules in your s3 bucket as well.
[04:37] Maria: If we need to purge a customer's historical conversation data, what's the workflow?
[04:43] Priya: There are two paths: automatic retention expiry and manual purge. for manual purge we have a purge API where you pass a customer id and optionally conversation ids; the system will delete all persisted blobs and mark the items as purged in the audit log.
[04:59] Priya: Purges generate a signed job id and you can track progress; if you're on Private you can choose to have the purge run entirely in your environment.
[05:12] Alex: How long does purge take? we have ~200k conversations.
[05:17] Priya: It depends on retention and storage tier. for hosted with object store, typical time is minutes to a few hours for that scale; for very large datasets we stream purge jobs and provide incremental progress. we'll include an SLA estimate for your dataset in the POC scoping.
[05:32] Tom: Do you keep backups that could rehydrate deleted data?
[05:36] Priya: Backups are part of the platform but they honor retention and purge requests; when purge is requested we scrub the primary and backup copies. we keep immutable snapshots only for a short RPO window unless you opt in.
[05:50] Jordan: circling back to data in transit \u2014 we support TLS everywhere and mTLS for Private endpoints, and you can require client certs for added assurance.
[05:59] Maria: For PCI, our auditors will want to see specific controls and the KMS attestation. do you provide artifact packs?
[06:07] Jordan: Yes, we have a security pack with SOC2, encryption details, key rotation docs, and a PCI control mapping. we'll send that after the call.
[06:16] Alex: Are there cost implications for retention disabled vs enabled? we are trying to model per-tenant TCO.
[06:23] Luis: Good question \u2014 storing request payloads increases storage and egress costs; Redwood Optimize can recommend caching/quantization and show unit economics per route. we can run a simulation for your traffic profile.
[06:36] Tom: speaking of Optimize, can it suggest retention policies per route based on pii risk?
[06:42] Priya: We're piloting a feature that recommends retention tiers based on detected PII and latency requirements. it's not yet GA but we can include a rough assessment in the POC.
[06:54] Maria: We need explicit controls for developers to opt-out of storing dev/test traffic to keep it out of logs.
[07:01] Priya: You can create policy templates for environments (prod/dev) and bind them to API keys so dev keys auto-apply do-not-store.
[07:11] Alex: Walk us through a sample trace where redaction occurs.
[07:15] Priya: Sure. i'll trigger a sample card number and email in the request. (typing) request sent.
[07:29] Priya: in the logs you can see [REDACTED_CC] and the classification score 0.97. the original field shows only in the secure dev vault for 15 minutes then it's purged unless retention set to store.
[07:45] Tom: that dev vault \u2014 who can access it?
[07:49] Priya: Access is limited via RBAC; by default only org admins and security roles can access. access requests are logged.
[07:59] Maria: For evidence to auditors we need a chain of custody for data deletion. do you emit signed events?
[08:06] Priya: Yes purge jobs emit signed events with job id, scope, timestamp, and operator; we can ship them to your event bus.
[08:15] Jordan: quick note on retention windows: you can set retention windows globally and override per-route. default options are 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, 1 year, never.
[08:28] Alex: We want a 30 day default but 0 retention for test tenants and strict do-not-store for cardholder data.
[08:36] Priya: That maps well to policy templates. we can also apply redaction rules that specifically target PCI patterns to ensure card numbers are always masked.
[08:47] Tom: any pitfalls with streaming responses and redaction? we stream tokens back to clients \u2014 do you redact on the fly?
[08:54] Priya: Streaming doesn't persist token-level payloads. redaction is applied at ingestion before storage; for streaming we can optionally perform on-the-fly masking for sensitive entities if you enable it, which may add a tiny latency delta.
[09:10] Maria: Latency is a concern; we need sub-200ms p95 for some flows. what is the overhead of enabling redaction?
[09:17] Priya: For most requests the overhead is low (<10ms) for regex and <30ms for ML detection at typical sizes. for high throughput paths we recommend routing to Dedicated where you get predictable latency and can run redaction closer to the inference nodes.
[09:34] Jordan: we'll note latency targets in the POC scoping doc.
[09:38] Alex: Show us how the API header works again.
[09:41] Priya: (switching to API tab) here is a curl example: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "x-redwood-store: never" \
  -d '{"input": "please charge card 4111 1111 1111 1111 for amount"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer
[09:58] Priya: server side the request flows through the scrubber, then the detector, then the model; if never is set, the scrubbed payload is not persisted.
[10:08] Tom: How do we prove the header was honored? we need an attestation or logs that show it was set.
[10:14] Priya: The audit log includes request headers and the evaluation outcome but not the plaintext payload. it records x-redwood-store: never and a hash of the request id; you can correlate that to the billing record.
[10:27] Maria: what about third-party plugins or tools that do callbacks? do you persist webhook payloads?
[10:33] Priya: Webhook callbacks are configurable; by default we do not persist webhook bodies unless you opt in. you can set different retention for outbound hooks.
[10:43] Alex: Can we demo the purge API?
[10:46] Priya: Yes \u2014 i'll call the purge endpoint for a demo tenant id demo-acme-01. (typing) request submitted.
[10:56] Priya: you can see the job id: purge-job-20260225-0007 and status: queued. we'll stream updates to the UI.
[11:06] Tom: i see the event in the audit stream. can we see the signed event payload?
[11:10] Priya: (click) here is the signed event in the audit export: { job_id: purge-job-20260225-0007, scope: tenant demo-acme-01, operator: priya.n@redwood.ai, timestamp: 2026-02-25T22:10Z, signature: <sig> }
[11:28] Alex: good. for our POC, we want to test a 30 day retention with automatic purge and ensure no cardholder data is ever stored.
[11:36] Jordan: we'll scope that \u2014 run simulated traffic and a short live run with dev keys and production keys.
[11:42] Maria: we may want to have a security review before the POC go-ahead. can you share architecture diagrams?
[11:48] Jordan: yes we'll attach architecture & threat model and the security artifact pack.
[11:53] Priya: quick note on Private deployment: if you require air-gapped or on-prem, we support that \u2014 data remains in your network and you manage disk storage lifecycle. that option is common for regulated payments customers.
[12:07] Tom: any changes to API for Private?
[12:10] Priya: API surface is identical; routing and key management differ. we provide deployment manifests and support for your infra team.
[12:18] Alex: ok let's talk timelines: we want a POC by end of March.
[12:23] Jordan: doable \u2014 we'll follow up with a scoping doc and proposed timeline.
[12:29] Luis: we'll include a simulation of retention costs per-tenant and expected throughput.
[12:35] Maria: Also need clarity on data residency if we move to Dedicated in different cloud regions.
[12:41] Priya: you can pin region and have separate storage buckets per region; we can enforce region-bound storage via policy.
[12:52] Alex: Any known limits on purge frequency? we might have many legal requests.
[12:58] Priya: No hard limit but heavy churn may affect throughput; for high-volume purge requests we suggest a scheduled job model and rate-limited queue which we can size for you.
[13:12] Tom: For QA \u2014 can developers replay requests in a sandbox without exposing real data?
[13:18] Priya: Yes, we provide a redaction-only view and a synthetic replay tool that can mask or synthesize PII for debugging.
[13:28] Jordan: wrapping up demo, quick Q&A?
[13:32] Alex: How much engineering effort to get keys integrated with our KMS?
[13:36] Priya: Low; typical integration is a few hours to set up grant and IAM roles for AWS KMS; for HSMs we'll need a little longer due to network controls. we'll provide a runbook.
[13:48] Maria: Can we get an NDA or enough to share sample logs?
[13:52] Jordan: We have an NDA template; we'll send it and can do a redacted log sample with the NDA in place.
[13:59] Alex: sounds good.
[14:02] Jordan: thank you all, next we'll compile POC scoping with timelines and security pack.
[14:08] Priya: thanks.
[14:12] (call ends)

Notes: Transcript includes ocasional typos and imperfect transcription (e.g., piI / PII, some names spelled differently). The meeting lasted ~42 minutes and included a live demo of Console toggles, API header behavior, purge job, and audit exports.
